skill.name: ascii-visualizer
skill.description: Creates clear ASCII diagrams for architectures, plans, workflows, comparisons, progress, and file structures.
skill.summary: Turn complex technical information into compact, readable ASCII visualizations.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: All 16 static findings are false positives. The two architecture findings cite ordinary diagram labels, while the 14 command findings are Markdown fences surrounding static ASCII examples.

static_findings.snippet: State Management     Zustand + RQ        Hybrid pattern 🎯

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 127 is static diagram text describing a memoized hook and responsive grid. It contains no system reconnaissance instruction or operation.
Line 333 is a comparison row naming Zustand and React Query state management. It does not request or perform system reconnaissance.
Lines 10 through 12 are a fenced Markdown example of an activation announcement. No Ruby, shell command, or executable backtick expression is present.
The detected token is a Markdown fence between prose sections. The surrounding content contains usage guidance and no executable command.
Line 29 opens a fenced ASCII box diagram. The fence contains only box-drawing characters and component labels.
Line 39 closes a fenced ASCII box diagram before the file-tree heading. It is Markdown formatting, not shell execution.
Line 42 opens a static file-tree example. The enclosed paths and labels are illustrative text with no command syntax.
Line 57 closes the static file-tree example. It is a Markdown fence and does not invoke an external process.
Line 60 opens a static flow-chart example. The enclosed text only illustrates data flow between named components.
Line 71 closes the static flow chart before a comparison heading. No shell or Ruby expression appears in this range.
Line 74 opens a static ASCII comparison table. Its contents are display labels and example metrics, not executable commands.
Line 83 closes the static comparison table. The backticks are a Markdown fence with no command execution context.
Line 86 opens a static progress-bar example. The enclosed project labels and percentages are presentation text only.
Line 94 closes the static progress-bar example. It is Markdown formatting and cannot execute a command.
Line 98 opens a reference block containing box-drawing characters, arrows, and status symbols. It has no Ruby or shell code.
Line 112 closes the box-drawing character reference. The following lines are prose best practices and usage examples, not commands.

content.value_statement: Complex technical explanations can be difficult to scan in plain prose. This skill converts them into compact ASCII diagrams with consistent visual structure.
actual_capabilities: Creates box diagrams for components and relationships.
Builds file trees for project and module structures.
Visualizes workflows and data flows with directional arrows.
Formats comparisons as aligned ASCII tables.
Represents progress and status with text bars and symbols.
Produces layered architecture explanations from high-level views to detailed flows.
limitations: Does not create rendered images or interactive diagrams.
Does not inspect repositories or verify supplied architecture facts.
Complex diagrams may wrap in narrow displays or proportional fonts.
Does not replace code syntax highlighting or standard Markdown tables.

use_cases.title: Explain a system architecture
use_cases.description: Convert services, data stores, and integrations into a readable component diagram.

use_cases.title: Present an implementation workflow
use_cases.description: Show ordered phases, ownership, dependencies, and completion states in one visual flow.

use_cases.title: Document a project structure
use_cases.description: Turn folders and key files into an annotated tree for onboarding documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Simple process flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a compact ASCII flow for this process: [steps]. Label each stage and show direction clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a visual sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Project file tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an annotated ASCII file tree from this structure: [folders and files]. Add one short purpose beside each important item.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is documenting repository organization.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] in an aligned ASCII visualization. Include architecture, benefits, tradeoffs, and recommended use cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is evaluating two technical approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Layered system design
prompt_templates.prompt: Visualize this system at three levels: context, components, and data flow. Use consistent symbols and keep each diagram within 100 columns: [details].
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect needs a detailed design review artifact.

output_examples.input: Show how a browser request reaches the application database.
output_examples.output: A left-to-right flow connects Browser, Load Balancer, API, Service, and Database, with response direction shown below.

output_examples.input: Compare the current monolith with a proposed modular architecture.
output_examples.output: An aligned before-and-after comparison shows component count, dependency boundaries, deployment model, and migration impact.

output_examples.input: Document the main folders in a web application.
output_examples.output: An annotated tree lists application routes, feature modules, shared components, integrations, state, styles, and global types.

best_practices: Provide accurate labels, relationships, and ordering before requesting a diagram.
Keep diagrams within 80 to 100 columns for reliable display.
Use one consistent set of borders, arrows, and status symbols.
anti_patterns: Do not use ASCII diagrams when a standard table communicates the data more clearly.
Do not place long paragraphs inside narrow boxes.
Do not imply that visualized metrics or architecture details were independently verified.

faq.question: What types of visuals can this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates architecture diagrams, workflows, file trees, comparisons, progress bars, and layered data-flow views.

faq.question: Can it generate image files?
faq.answer: No. It produces text-based ASCII visualizations for terminals, chat, and Markdown documents.

faq.question: Does it analyze my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. Supply the relevant folders, components, relationships, and facts in your prompt.

faq.question: Will diagrams display correctly everywhere?
faq.answer: They display best with a monospaced font. Narrow screens may wrap wide diagrams.

faq.question: Can it show implementation status?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add progress bars, completion markers, priorities, and phase labels.

faq.question: Which assistants support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
